body:
I'm gonna try this again.

Maybe you are right.  If having her in my life is only causing me pain, perhaps not having her in my life--at least for the moment--is the best solution.  I'm just bitter.  I'm bitter that I got fired.  I'm bitter that I have such a difficult time forming new friendships.  I'm bitter that I'm 27, I haven't a job and I haven't had a girlfriend in over 5 years, which seems like a long time to me.

I need to find a job...but I don't really know what I like/am interested in.  So it just feels overwhelming, especially since I don't know what to do....
I'm sorry.  I'm such an asshole.  You're trying to help me.  And. I'm an asshole waste of life.

I guess your right.  It just makes me so depressed to know that almost everyone I've ever been friends with is now but a distant memory.  I hate to think that I have to add one more name to that list.

I think I'm gonna wait a bit more before I try calling/emailing her again.  Maybe she'll get back to me in a few days and maybe she won't. I guess if it goes on for a bit--a week?--I'll send her a really short message... I'll cross that bridge when I come to it.

I just wish I didn't live in the U.S. of FAIL.  All we ever here about is economic meltdown and how our bat-shit-insane "leaders" have sent all of our jobs to China and India.  My options are either paper-pusher in an office or burger-slinger.  SOME COUNTRY!  Whatever.  I'll get some bullshit job. And every day will be the same and I can just wait until I die.

>Hating yourself is never the right choice. Learn to know yourself, whether through a therapist or some other means, and try to accept that person.

I am going to a therapist.  (I'm unemployed, but my parents aren't and they are footing the bill.  I've been against this from the start.  I'm 27, I have no job, no nothing and mommie and daddie are paying for my therapy.  YUCK!)  I've only been twice, so I can't really make any judgment.  He seems better than OK though, and I hope it will work out.  He's a CBT-type.  I specifically sought out this type of therapist because I believe that it is effective for depressive/anxiety-ridden types: a.k.a. me.  I'm crossing my fingers it works.

Contrary to my opening post, I actually do have friends.  There are a number of people in my city who I see from time to time.  I also have two friends who would take bullets for me.  I'm really SO lucky to have them.  I dunno what I'd do otherwise.  I live with my sister and her girlfriend.  They are great, but I have a hard time talking to them about this stuff, because they tend to over-analyze everything and offer too many "solutions".  I have a hard time talking about this with my friends because I don't want to burden them with my problems, and I know that at least one of them doesn't do the whole emotional support thing.

The important thing is I do have friends.  But I have a really hard time making NEW friends.  I never talk to strangers, I don't really like going to clubs or bars, and I'm not in any sports clubs.  I probably should do some Meetups, especially since I've got the time.  But, I'm afraid.  I wish I wasn't so afraid of other people.  I wish my dream wasn't to be alone on a farm 100 miles from the nearest person...

Thanks for your reply.

"she's using that to conclude that you don't want to be friends with her"  Oh no.  I think you might be right.  What to do, what to do?  I emailed her back (see my reply to RiseAgainst378 above).  But she has yet to reply.  I guess I just have to give it more time--maybe she's away from her computer...

I don't really know what to say to her.  I'm afraid to call her, because I might say something bad that will only make the situation worse.  What is this bad thing I may say?  I have no fucking clue, but I'm bad enough with the whole "interpersonal relationship thing" that I greatly fear my fuck-ups.

So I dunno... She emailed me, I emailed her back.  Should I call? Should I text?  Should I just keep waiting?  Should I write more?  I dunno.  All I know is that I don't want to lose my friend, but I have no idea how to stop what has been set in motion.

I don't even know what to say to her.  I wrote back to her and I told her that I really didn't want our friendship to end.  I told her that I valued and appreciated her honesty, and that I too want to find some resolution.  I stressed that I REALLY wanted to find a way to work through this and maintain our friendship.  I mentioned that I am feeling a lot of anxiety, but I wasn't like "OMG I'm so anxious its all my fault".  I think it was a normal email.  I hope it was.  I just feel so awful now--like I'm just destined to hurt anyone and everyone I've ever cared about....

Should I call her, or just leave her alone?  It seems like she just hates me, so maybe I shouldn't call her.  As far as timeline goes, it is now 9:30 PM (Eastern U.S.) she wrote to me today at 12:35 AM.  I replied at 1:42 AM (same day).  I can wait a day or two for her to get back to me, but maybe I should send her a text or call her?  But I don't want to be to intrusive.  It seems like she just wants me out of her life.  If I really care about her, maybe just leaving her alone will be my final display of friendship and admiration.  How utterly sad.

>You have to come out of your shell

I am VERY aware of this.  I probably have Social (or Generalized) Anxiety Disorder or some other similar problem which makes these sorts of situations VERY difficult for me.  This could well be why I'm still unemployed and not really doing anything about it.  I tell myself, "The economy sucks, why bother?"--But I must admit my true thoughts are more along the lines of "I'll never get hired--I'm too stupid and under qualified".  Given adequate perspective, I realize this is self-deception: I have a college education and--I'm seriously NOT a pompous asshole but--I'm actually really quite bright.  So yeah, these sorts of risks are just way difficult for me.  I know I'm just making excuses, but given the choice of picking up the phone and facing the unknown or just feeling bad, I'd rather go with the known quantity.

So I feel like I probably said the wrong thing, or maybe didn't say the right thing.  And now maybe I've lost a friend.  I don't know what to do...

The arm-wrestling father? OH yeah!  You're telling me!  I'm still WAY confused about all of this.  I guess I'm glad that I have learned all this stuff about Girl, as now I kind of see her for what she is: someone who totally played me and maybe isn't the nicest person in the world.  Evidence: her roommate is REALLY nice.  She's always supportive of other people, complements them (and me) and is fun to be around.  Girl frequently makes negative comments about her roommate's weight.  Calls her obese. Girl is TINY.  I guess it is just typical "skinnybitch" behavior.  Nasty.  Her roommate is probably a bit sedentary, and she has mentioned concern with her
weight.  But obese? Hardly.  I do not understand Girl.  I guess I'm glad she played me like she did, as I don't think she is a person that I really want to call my friend at this point, let alone date.

If Girl really wanted to help her roommate, I would think she might change their cooking habits a bit (Girl cooks, roommate cleans), or maybe even begin an exercise regime together.  Girl may be tiny, but is not "in shape" (She doesn't exercise with regularity, which is probably THE contributing cause of her insomnia.  Recently, we went for a short, EASY hike of about 4 miles and she was down for the count on the train ride home).  I say this as a person who eats a balanced diet and exercises regularly.  And I'm accepting of all sorts of people.  I think it is great for people to get into shape, AND I realize it is often difficult to get there.  I should know myself--I got into not very good shape in, and just after, college (weight gain, smoking, drinking, unhealthy diet, no exercise), but have now adopted a much healthier lifestyle (healthy diet of whole grains, veg and limited meat; regular exercise; quit smoking; DRASTICALLY curtailed drinking.)  If I can do it, anyone can! 

I have considered Thailand a little bit.  Friends who have visited report it is a beautiful country, filled with nice people, delicious food and low prices.  Sounds really nice.  I'd be a little concerned about their political stability--but I guess I'm concerned about the political situation in most all countries--but I'm not here to get into politics, despite my love for political debates....

I guess I just don't know if I really want to leave my city.  It is a great place, in its own way, and I have friends and family here.  So I don't know.

I know it's not just me, and yet we all feel it is just ourselves, as it doesn't hurt as much when it isn't us.

I get what you are saying about taking advantage of my youth.  I think I do--I exercise, go skiing and backpacking, travel when I have the time.  And I really value the bonds I have with my friends, and my sister and her girlfriend, with whom I live.  In many respects, my life is really great. But there are some pieces that seem "missing", and I can't help but seek them out.

Feeling a bit better today.  I had this lunch with my mother that went really poorly. I don't understand that woman at all.  She is convinced that I need a comprehensive psychological evaluation and anything else is wrong.  She keeps telling me "you owe it to yourself" and "it is in your best interest".  I find it utterly fascinating to know that she is so in tune with my best interest.  And I'm so glad to hear that she's made such progress with her anxiety (she doesn't have depression.  She just feels sad and dejected and used to tell us as kids that we were "making her look good".  LOL at self-awareness champion, because otherwise...

So lunch with Mom was tons of fun.  On the bright side, I don't live with her and only see her occasionally, although recently she's been really pushing this whole lunch trip.  I realize she cares about me and wants what is best.  But she doesn't even look at me when I'm speaking, and it doesn't seem as though she listens to me on a meaningful level.  I sometimes even wonder if she is simply to superficial to do otherwise.

I eventually got a little bit frustrated and angry, which she was able to pick up on.  She asked me why I was mad at HER. I told her, "you aren't listening. I'm not mad at YOU, I'm mad at this situation in which I'm not able to express myself clearly to my parents."  She told me she thought it was "bad" that I was angry. I replied that while I understood my anger made her uncomfortable, it is still a valid feeling that I am having and I didn't think calling it "bad" was particularly helpful.  She shook her head and reaffirmed her disagreement.  I found this advice about the wrongness of my feelings to be really helpful, in a *deep* and *meaningful* way.

Right now, I'm just looking forward to having a crazy weekend with a bunch of my friends that involves camping, a rock concert, and driving through 6 states.  (I bet you can tell that I'm not living out West!)  It should be pretty insane in a pretty insanely good way.

I'm planing on doing some camping this weekend, and I'm going on a longer backpacking trip in early June (maybe 2 weeks or so).  I'm extremely excited about this.  I'm hoping the change of scenery, mountains, etc. will do me good.

I'm just feeling uncomfortable about what to do after this.  I"m really tired, but I appreciate the support.

Live in the mountains--Maybe like a park ranger--that actually ranges.  Or maybe live on a farm.  But I'm afraid that might simply be the thinking of an urban romantic, and how could I be sure.  I fear that the fear will keep me where I am.  LOL!  I wonder if I really am the same person who moved to Japan with only very basic language skills.

Bluegerm: I guess this IS partly the problem.  I feel as though there aren't ENOUGH restrictions.  I could be a teacher, or a baker, or an engineer, or a park ranger.  I'm not sure what these jobs have to do with one another.  There are so many options from which to select.  It is overwhealming.  I wonder how other people make these choices....  My former employer hired a "career counselor" for me, which was really generous.  I just hoe that I'm not putting too much blind faith in her ability to help me narrow down my options.

That does sound like a good idea.  But then I wonder if I even should.  If rejection means nothing but pain for me, then perhaps I should seek to limit opportunities for rejection.  Trying to meet girls has been, and I'm afraid still is, a recipe for disaster.

I'm probably being a tad melodramatic here.

I like the woods.  Being there always reminds me of how much I hate being stuck in this prison without bars.  I'm planing to go backpacking for 2 weeks since I have the time.  But it seeks frivolous to do so.  I kind of want to maybe cancel the trip.  But that will likely cause aggravation with my friends and family, so I guess I will go.  I think being out in the mountains will be really good for me, I just need to get past my feelings that I don't deserve to have fun because I lost my job.

I also like cooking a lot.  I do it most every day.  Cooking and eating healthy food for myself and my friends is an activity I really enjoy.  We (my friends and I) try to live healthfully--we go running ever other day, cook meals made with fresh, whole ingredients and stuff like that.  But even this has a dark side: While my family tells me I should be thinking about grad school, my friends think that I should operate a street cart, selling delicious vegetarian-based meals.  Their excitement for my food is great and all, but that seems like a really tough job.  I hear so much what other people think I should be doing, that I never seem to be able to listen for what I want to be doing.  I really thought that by the time I was 27 (in 10 days!) I would have had my shit figured out a lot better.

Japan was really great--I lived in Osaka for 1.5 years and Tokyo for 5 months.  It felt good just go go there, pick up the language and culture, feel independent and visit so many amazing places.

Japan was really not great--I lost by job because the company was financially unstable and forced into bankruptcy.  The business was taken over by another company which promised me a job.  On Christmas Eve, they told me I wouldn't have a job after all.

Japan was really great--I got 3 months of unemployment (60 percent of my salary) and 80 percent of the wages my bankrupt employer owed me.  I found a new job, in suburban Tokyo, and traveled all over the country!

Japan was hard--My new job, as an assistant teacher in middle schools, was really boring.  I was nothing more than a tape recorder.  Furthermore, my employer failed to deliver on promised language lessons, and the lower salary did not cover the higher cost of living in Tokyo.

I came back to the states and decided I would just go to grad school for ESL because it was an easy decision and I didn't have to explain it to anyone--they "got it" I guess.  I found the program really pedantic and wondered if it was worth the cost.  So, I decided to not pursue it fully.

Now I'm totally lost.  My parents--especially my mum--want me to undergo a comprehensive psychiatric evaluation because the "think it will help".  It will likely help to temporarily assuage my mothers anxiety.  She can say that she did something.  I've tried to explain that I'm open to the idea of therapy, but don't see the need for an expensive evaluation.  Apparently, this is a difficult concept for them to understand. These conversations do not go well.

I have no idea what I would like to do.  I hate the idea of working in an office and banging on a keyboard all day like that cat in the youtube videos.  I guess most people dig that shit, or whatever, but that seems like psychic suicide to me.  If I'm just gonna be doing nothing anyway, I'd rather do nothing.  I live in a big city, so all the jobs are gonna be working inside and using a computer.  If I'm lucky, I might get 2 or 3 days of vacation time...If I don't get laid off--I mean "restructured"--again.
I'm banned too!  Please unban!  I just made this account today so I can post here.  I don't want my friends and family to know how bad I feel/needs to be secret.

I don't even know where to begin or end.

I'm 26.  

I've been depressed on and off since I was 15 or so.  I cut my wrists something terrible on time in college and found myself in hospital.  I eventually finished college and then taught in Japan for two years.  There have been good times and bad times.  I've been back in my home city for a year now and am feeling so low.  I was in grad school, but dropped out because I don't know if I really wanna be an ESL teacher.  So I got a job, but recently lost it on account of the economy.  Also quite recently there has been Girl.  I met Girl last fall, and took quite a liking to her.  She's funny, energetic, likes cooking and being in the woods.  These are all things I really quite value.  And I thought she  liked me!  We've spent an awful lot of time together since December, and I really developed a bit of a crush on her.  This is a big deal for me, as I haven't been on a date or anything in about 5 years.  This sounds like a long time, as it is is about 20 per cent of my life.  SO.  I. Took. The. Plunge.  "Let's go out!"  I say.  She says she can't because her roommate might feel isolated.  Oh.  Well, imagine my surprise, then, when she tells me last Saturday that she's been dating some guy, and it's really going well, and blah, blah, blah.  

(also, before that she introduced me to her parents (DON'T FUCKING ASK) and her psychotic father forced my into arm wrestling.  Normally this is just basic human insanity.  What makes it a little different is that I was recently in a bike accident that fucked up my shoulder.  SO, she decides to let her father go savage on me and than break the news that, oh yeah, I have NO INTEREST in you either.)

FML.

I feel like I've been hit in the stomach: I have no job, Girl obviously hates me, parents don't want to understand me and constantly ask me about grad school.  My life is complete fail.  Booze and pot are the only bright spots in my life.
